solves: Gathers a title, a description and short controls in a surface anchored to a trigger, so the person adjusts or decides something short without leaving the page.
use_when: When the person needs to adjust or decide something short without losing their place on the page, such as filtering, choosing a due date or renaming something.
Choose no arrow by default; use the arrow when the trigger sits among other elements and the link needs to be clear.
Choose the size by the content: sm for a short title and description, md when the footer or a field comes in, lg when the field needs more width.
Turn the footer on when the action needs confirmation; the divider comes with it.
Turn the close button on when there is no footer and the content asks for a visible way out besides Esc and a press outside, such as information to read calmly.
do_not_use_when: As a list of commands: use nph-dropdown-menu.
For a decision that blocks the page: use a modal dialog.
For a short notice with no action: use a short text next to the element, with no floating surface.
With two primary actions in the footer: use one primary solid and one secondary solid.
With an outlined trigger: use the secondary solid nph-button.
Inside a dialog: not part of the contract yet.

for.constraint: The id of the element that opens the popover, looked up in the same root as the popover, like the for of nph-tooltip and nph-dropdown-menu. The trigger stays outside the component. The popover writes aria-haspopup dialog, aria-expanded and aria-controls on it. A for that is empty or matches no element in that root draws nothing and emits console.error in development. A disabled, aria-disabled or loading trigger opens nothing.

open.constraint: The state. The trigger turns it on and off; the consumer may set it, and setting it to false is how a footer action closes the popover. Setting it from code never fires nph-close.

heading.constraint: The title, already localized. Always visible; it is the h2 of the surface and its accessible name. Empty draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

description.constraint: The support text below the title, in popover/description. It describes the surface for the screen reader. Empty draws no description.

side.constraint: Where the surface opens relative to the trigger. The popover turns to the opposite side when the one asked for does not fit and the opposite has more room, and never leaves the window. The side it resolved to is on the surface, not on the host, which keeps the value the consumer set. The sides are physical. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

align.constraint: How the surface aligns to the trigger on that side. On the top and bottom sides, start and end follow the writing direction; on the left and right sides, start is the top and end the bottom. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

arrow.constraint: An arrow that points to the trigger, decorative. Off by default. With the arrow, the surface sits one arrow height further from the trigger, so the tip keeps popover/offset from it.

size.constraint: 240, 320 or 400 wide. It changes only the width: margins, gaps and footer buttons stay the same, and the height follows the content. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

closable.constraint: Draws the close button, a compact ghost secondary nph-button with the xmark icon, 28 by 28. It needs close-label.

close-label.constraint: The accessible name of the close button, already localized, such as Close. Required while the button is shown; without it the popover draws without the button and emits console.error in development.

slot.constraint: The default slot is the body, an nph-field for instance. The footer slot takes the action buttons: a secondary solid and a primary solid compact nph-button. The divider comes with the footer; with no footer there is none.

nph-close.constraint: Bubbles, composed, cancelable, with detail source escape, outside, close-button or focus-out, fired before it closes when the person asks. preventDefault keeps it open. Setting open from code, the trigger and a footer action never fire it.

placement.choose_when: bottom, the default, unless the layout asks for another side; top, right or left when there is no room below or the context asks for it. center, the default, unless the surface should start or end where the trigger does. The popover turns to the opposite side by itself when the one asked for does not fit.
do_not_combine_with: a side or an alignment outside the lists

arrow.choose_when: Off, the default, because the link to the trigger is already clear by proximity and the drawing is cleaner; on when the trigger sits among other elements and the link needs to be clear.

size.choose_when: sm (240) for a short title and description; md (320), the default, when the footer or a field comes in; lg (400) when the field needs more width.
do_not_combine_with: a size to change margins, gaps or the footer buttons: the size changes only the width

parts.choose_when: Description on by default; body, close button and footer off by default. Turn the footer on when the action needs confirmation; turn the close button on when there is no footer and the content asks for a visible way out.
do_not_combine_with: two primary actions in the footer

open.changes_for_user: The surface shows anchored to the trigger, the trigger carries aria-expanded true and draws the hover-active look of its own component, and the focus goes into the surface.

trigger-open.changes_for_user: The nph-button trigger keeps the look of hover-active while the popover is open, even with the pointer away. It is an extra signal; aria-expanded is the one that says it is open.

business_rules: The popover is not modal: the page stays usable, nothing traps the Tab key, and it closes with Esc, a press outside, the close button, the footer action or the focus leaving it.

On close the focus goes back to the trigger when it was inside the popover and the person did not move it: Esc, the close button and the footer action give it back; a press outside and the focus leaving leave it where the person put it.
A footer action closes the popover because the consumer sets open to false in its handler; the popover fires no event for it.
Esc closes only the popover: it does not reach a dialog around it.
The footer is one divider, from edge to edge, in popover/divider, then the actions, compact, popover/footer-gap apart. On a touch screen the footer buttons go back to the default size.
The surface does not clip its content, so the focus ring of an inner piece is not cut.
The title is always visible and names the surface; the description describes it.
The trigger is an nph-button, secondary solid. Open, it takes the hover-active look and carries aria-expanded true, with aria-haspopup dialog and aria-controls.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the piece writes no word of its own.
domain_errors: A for that is empty or matches no element in the same root of the popover: it draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
An empty heading, or a side, an align or a size outside the lists: it draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.
closable with no close-label: it draws without the close button and emits console.error in development.

tokens.surface: popover/background, popover/foreground, popover/border, popover/border-width, popover/radius, elevation/dropdown

ai_hints: Use nph-popover to adjust or decide something short without leaving the page; for a list of commands use nph-dropdown-menu, for a decision that blocks the page use a modal dialog.
Give for with the id of the trigger, an nph-button secondary solid, and heading with a short title that states the decision.
Keep a single primary action, at the end of the footer: a secondary solid and a primary solid, compact.
Close it from the footer action by setting open to false in the handler of the button.
Prefer no arrow; use it only when the trigger sits among other elements.
Turn the close button on, with close-label, when there is no footer.
Do not put a popover inside a dialog: it is not part of the contract yet.

accessibility.semantics: The surface is a non-modal dialog, named by the title through aria-labelledby and described by the description through aria-describedby. The trigger carries aria-haspopup dialog, aria-expanded and aria-controls, the last one pointing to the popover host, because an id reference does not cross a shadow root. When the trigger is an nph-button, the native button inside it carries aria-haspopup and aria-expanded. The arrow is decorative (aria-hidden).
accessibility.accessible_name: The surface: heading. The description: description. The close button: close-label. The trigger: its own text or aria-label.
keyboard: Enter and Space on the trigger open the popover; the focus goes into it by the focus rule.
Esc closes it and gives the focus back to the trigger, and does not reach a dialog around it.
Tab moves through the body and the footer in order and then on to the page; the focus leaving the popover closes it.
accessibility.focus: Each inner piece shows the focus ring of its own component; the surface takes no ring. On open, the focus goes to the first element with autofocus, otherwise to the first focusable element of the body, then of the footer, then to the close button, then to the surface itself.
accessibility.contrast: Title and description pass 4.5:1 over the surface in both themes. The border and the divider are decorative: in light the surface stands apart by the shadow, in dark by the lighter background.
accessibility.color_alternative: Open, the surface shows anchored to the trigger and the trigger carries aria-expanded true; the hover-active look of the trigger is an extra signal, not the only one.

invalid_combinations: closable without close-label — the close button has an icon and no text.
A side, an align or a size outside the lists.
A for that matches no element in the same root as the popover.
Two primary actions in the footer — use one primary solid and one secondary solid.

parents: a page, a toolbar, a table row or a card, next to its trigger

anti_patterns: Using the popover as a list of commands, as a modal dialog or as a short notice.
Using an outlined trigger, or a trigger that is not an nph-button.
Putting two primary actions in the footer.
Putting an nph-card inside the popover: its parts are its own.
Leaving the trigger without an accessible name.
Drawing a divider with no footer.
